methodology.title: How we estimate sales
methodology.intro: Publishers rarely announce their sales. But every game leaves public traces. We track them, compare them with what we know about other games, and turn them into an estimate.
methodology.recipeBody1: The best-known way to guess a game's sales fits in one line: take its number of Steam reviews and multiply it. But the same number of reviews doesn't mean the same thing for a 2018 game and for one released last week, or for a PC exclusive and a console hit.
methodology.recipeBody2: So we went further, with an approach that takes each game's profile into account.
methodology.signalsBody: Our catalog follows more than 6,000 games, through more than 2.6 million public data points:
methodology.signalReviews: Steam reviews: how many and how fast, at launch and today
methodology.signalProfile: The game's profile: age, platforms, multiplayer, live service, annual release, late PC release
methodology.signalTrackRecord: The track record of its series and studio
methodology.similarTitle: Every game is compared with its peers
methodology.similarBody1: No game can be understood on its own. For each one, we look for the games most like it in our library of more than 2,000 reference games: same kind of game, same scale, same era.
methodology.similarBody2: Their history tells us how many sales a review represents in that family of games, how their sales evolve after launch, and how much of them happen on PC.
methodology.figuresTitle: A base of more than 5,000 published figures
methodology.figuresBody1: We have gathered more than 5,000 public sales figures across more than 2,000 games, including publisher announcements, specialist press articles and data from analyst firms. They feed our reference games and are used to train our estimation model. Every figure is dated: the model only sees what was known on that date, never how the story continued.
methodology.figuresBody2: These figures also go through quality control: duplicates, misattributed editions and wrong dates are tracked down, and inconsistent figures are left out of training.
methodology.readBody: Our figures are estimates, not official sales: a publisher announcement never replaces our estimate. They change with the data, upward as well as downward if new information corrects the picture.
methodology.notEstimatedTitle: Where we prefer to show nothing
methodology.notEstimatedOld: Games released before 2017: data from that era doesn't let us reach the level of reliability we aim for.
methodology.notEstimatedFree: Free-to-play games: without a purchase, there are no copies to count.
methodology.notEstimatedPlatforms: Nintendo Switch and mobile: without a reliable signal, we don't give them a line of their own.
methodology.examplesBody: Each game page shows the figure, its split by platform and the signals we track:
methodology.examplesBlog: Read our articles on official sales
methodology.notEstimatedBody: We would rather show "not estimated" than a figure we don't believe in.
methodology.notEstimatedUnreleased: Games not out yet: with no sales, there is nothing to estimate. Data arrives at launch, and the first estimate a few days later.

gta6Sales.title: GTA 6 sales tracker
gta6Sales.metaTitle: GTA 6 sales: how many copies has GTA 6 sold?
gta6Sales.metaDescription: Every official GTA 6 sales figure since launch, with its source, compared with GTA V and Red Dead Redemption 2 over their first weeks.
gta6Sales.leadUpcoming: GTA 6 launches on {date}, in {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}. No sales figure exists yet: this page will log each official one as soon as it is published.
gta6Sales.leadAwaiting: GTA 6 launched on {date}. Rockstar and Take-Two have not published a sales figure yet: this page logs each one as soon as it comes out.
gta6Sales.leadLatest: GTA 6 has sold {units} copies, according to the latest official figure ({date}).
gta6Sales.intro: We only list figures with a public source: Take-Two, Rockstar and recognised market trackers. Each one is dated and linked.
gta6Sales.chartTitle: GTA 6 against GTA V and RDR2
gta6Sales.chartBody: Copies shipped worldwide by days since launch. Each point is an official Take-Two figure; the GTA 6 line grows as figures come out.
gta6Sales.chartAria: Copies sold by days since launch for GTA 6, GTA V and Red Dead Redemption 2
gta6Sales.figuresNone: No figure yet. For GTA V, Take-Two announced $1 billion in sales three days after launch, and its first unit count six weeks later. For RDR2, the first count came 12 days after launch.
gta6Sales.benchmarksTitle: What GTA V and RDR2 did
gta6Sales.benchmarksBody: Take-Two's reports for its two previous Rockstar launches, the only comparable ones.
gta6Sales.sourceTakeTwo: Take-Two's quarterly results, which give the units shipped for its big launches.
gta6Sales.sourceRockstar: Rockstar and Take-Two announcements, usually within days of a record launch.
gta6Sales.sourceAlinea: Alinea Analytics, a market tracker that publishes console sales figures within weeks of a launch.
gta6Sales.sourceCharts: Sales and download charts: Circana in the United States, GfK in the United Kingdom, Famitsu in Japan, and the PlayStation Store.
gta6Sales.sellIn: Take-Two counts copies "sold-in": shipped to stores, digital sales included, rather than only copies bought by players. It is the figure the publisher reports, and the one used for GTA V and RDR2 here.
gta6Sales.noModelTitle: Why no estimate of our own
gta6Sales.noModelBody: Our estimates rely mostly on Steam signals. GTA 6 launches on consoles only, and no game before it reached this scale, so a model would only guess. We show the published figures and their sources instead.
gta6Sales.gamePageLink: Follow GTA 6 sales figure by figure, against GTA V and RDR2

about.title: About Game Sales Tracker
about.intro: Game Sales Tracker answers a simple question: how many copies has this game sold? Publishers rarely share their sales. So every day we estimate the sales of more than 6,000 games on PC, PlayStation and Xbox, from public data.
about.offerGames: A page for every game, with its sales estimate, the split by platform and the known official figures, dated and sourced
about.offerHubs: Rankings by studio, publisher, franchise and release year
about.offerBlog: A blog that looks back at the official sales announced by publishers
about.sourcesBody: We follow the public traces every game leaves: Steam reviews, concurrent players, PlayStation Store and Xbox Store ratings, Steam followers. We compare them with a base of more than 5,000 published sales figures for more than 2,000 games.
about.whoBody: Game Sales Tracker is an independent project, built and maintained by {name}. It is not affiliated with any publisher, studio or console maker.
about.fundingBody: The site is free and needs no account. It is funded by advertising and by affiliate links to the Instant Gaming store. Neither has any influence on our estimates, and no publisher can pay to appear on the site or to have a figure changed.
about.contactLink: Write to us from the Contact page

contact.title: Contact
contact.intro: A question, a correction or a proposal? Write to us:
contact.correctionsTitle: Report an error or an official figure
contact.correctionsBody: Tell us which game it is about and include a link to the source: a publisher announcement, a financial report or a press article. We check every source before adding it. An official figure is added as reference data, with its date, but it does not replace the estimate.
contact.studiosBody: Have you announced a sales figure that is missing from your game's page? Send us the link to the announcement.
contact.pressBody: You can quote our figures by crediting Game Sales Tracker with a link to the game page. For a partnership or a sponsored placement, write to the same address.
contact.responseTime: We usually reply within a few days.

mw4Sales.title: Modern Warfare 4 sales tracker
mw4Sales.metaTitle: MW4 sales: how well is Modern Warfare 4 selling?
mw4Sales.metaDescription: Activision publishes no Modern Warfare 4 sales figure. We compare its Steam reviews with Black Ops 7 and Black Ops 6 at the same age, day by day since launch.
mw4Sales.leadComparison: No official sales figure exists for Modern Warfare 4. {day, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} after its PC launch, it has {reviews} Steam reviews, {ratio} times as many as Black Ops 7 at the same age.
mw4Sales.leadReviews: No official sales figure exists for Modern Warfare 4. {day, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} after its PC launch, it has {reviews} Steam reviews.
mw4Sales.leadNone: No official sales figure exists for Modern Warfare 4, and its Steam reviews are not available yet.
mw4Sales.intro: Each Call of Duty since Modern Warfare II runs inside the Call of Duty HQ launcher, which hides how many people play each title. The Steam reviews on each game's own store page still count that game alone: we compare them launch against launch.
mw4Sales.chartTitle: MW4 against Black Ops 7 and Black Ops 6
mw4Sales.chartBody: Steam reviews of each game's own page, by days since its PC launch. MW4 is read every day; for the older games we have the total at the end of each month, placed at the day it measured.
mw4Sales.chartAria: Steam reviews by days since launch for Modern Warfare 4, Black Ops 7 and Black Ops 6
mw4Sales.noFigureTitle: Why there is no sales figure
mw4Sales.noFigureBody: Activision has not given unit sales for a Call of Duty in years. On Steam, every recent title is played through the Call of Duty HQ app, so the player count of MW4's own page stays near zero, and on PlayStation its ratings are shared with the whole series. With no signal that measures MW4 alone, our model publishes no estimate for it. The reviews below are the one count that remains per game.
mw4Sales.caveatNotSales: A review is not a sale. The ratio says which launch is bigger on Steam, not how many copies were sold.
mw4Sales.caveatPcOnly: Steam is PC only. Most Call of Duty players are on PlayStation and Xbox, and many play through Game Pass.
mw4Sales.caveatReception: A badly received game draws more reviews per buyer: Black Ops 7 was mostly negative, which makes it look bigger than it was.
mw4Sales.caveatYears: Players write more reviews every year, so a recent game starts ahead of an older one with the same sales.
mw4Sales.caveatStopped: Black Ops 6's page stopped counting reviews in 2026, and Modern Warfare III's counts none, so they end there or are left out.
mw4Sales.figuresNone: None yet. Activision usually announces records (biggest launch, hours played) rather than copies; market trackers such as Circana and Alinea Analytics publish rankings and estimates within weeks. Each one will be listed here with its source.
mw4Sales.gamePageLink: No sales figure for MW4: compare its launch with Black Ops 7 and Black Ops 6
